avoidable_by: checking 'rustfmt --check' against the whole crate BEFORE running any fmt command on a shared/huge codebase; this repo's src/rules_core/pilot_compute/mod.rs is not itself rustfmt-clean, so any fmt invocation reformats far more than the touched lines
cause: ran 'cargo fmt -- <2 files>' which walked the whole crate's mod-tree and reformatted ~792 unrelated files (10508-line diff on mod.rs alone, project is not rustfmt-clean); had to git checkout -- . and redo all edits by hand
cost: one redo pass, ~15 Edit calls repeated
summary: cargo fmt scoped to 2 files still reformatted ~792 files via cargo's package-wide fmt behavior; discarded and redid by hand, no formatter used thereafter

actors_affected: any lane agent in a multi-lane wave that writes a long-running command's output to the shared scratchpad path
detected_by: self, noticing a non-monotonic test-count regression before trusting it in a final report
impact: full test-suite verification log corrupted by a cross-lane collision: wrote cargo test output to the harness-provided per-session scratchpad dir ($SCRATCHPAD/full_test_run.log); a SIBLING wave lane (a different worktree, wf_be4660f2-72a-1) wrote its own 'cargo test -j 8 --workspace' output to the EXACT SAME path -- lsof confirmed two tee processes (different PIDs, different worktree cwds) both holding fd 3w open on the same inode. The scratchpad dir the harness names 'session-specific, isolated' is apparently shared across every lane agent spawned under one orchestrator session, not private per lane-agent. Symptom: grep -c 'test result:' on the log fluctuated non-monotonically (517 -> 53) and wc -l dropped from 4514 to 173 lines between checks, both writers interleaving.
resolution: killed my own cargo test + tee, restarted with output redirected to a path inside my own CARGO_TARGET_DIR instead of the shared scratchpad, which is unique per lane by construction
